title: Profile rollforward and stable pin policy
creator: Avery Thompson
description: Define and implement a rollforward-first policy for Redwood-verified performance profiles that preserves pinned model behavior while enabling safe, auditable updates. Deliverables include a signed profile manifest format, automated rollforward gating rules (canary metrics + regression thresholds), TTL-based stale profile handling, and a self-service operator flow to promote emergency rollbacks. The goal is to reduce manual intervention for profile updates, lower risk of silent regressions in latency/throughput/cost, and provide a clear audit trail for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Profile manifest is signed and stored in the performance-catalog; signature verification occurs on publish and at runtime fallback checks.
Automated rollforward pipeline runs verification benchmarks and only promotes profiles if canary metrics (latency P95, throughput, and token-cost delta) are within configured thresholds.
Profiles include a stable-pin flag that prevents auto-rollforward for customer-pinned model versions; pinning flow documented and surfaced in Console.
Stale profiles auto-expire after configurable TTL (default 90 days) with a notification and soft-deprecation state before removal.
Emergency rollback path is operable from Console and CLI; rollbacks create a new signed manifest (opaque history) and emit audit log entries.
End-to-end telemetry exists for profile publish, canary evaluation, rollforward/rollback events, and user-facing status in the Console dashboard.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration verified for profile signing keys.
notes_and_progress: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng (runtime + infra), DX, and Security. Agreed scope: manifest signing + rollforward pipeline + Console UX for pins.
2026-03-04: Eng proposal accepted: use an append-only git-backed registry for manifests with commit signatures via KMS. Trade-off: slightly higher latency for profile lookup vs strong auditability.
2026-03-05: Decided on default TTL=90 days after product review; operators can override per-model. Will surface in profile metadata as expiry_date.

2026-03-06: Canary gating thresholds proposed: latency P95 increase <= 2.5%, throughput decrease <= 5%, token-cost delta <= +3%. These numbers are conservative; will iterate after 2 weeks of live canaries.
2026-03-07: Security reviewed signing approach; requirement to rotate signing keys every 6 months added to implementation tasks.
2026-03-09: UX draft for Console pin/unpin flow created; needs PM/Design review and copy edits. Inline warning copy must convey SLA and cost implications.
2026-03-10: Created GitHub draft PR for publish pipeline (refs: gh.com/redwood-inference/perf-catalog#321). Eng estimate 3 wks for pipeline + 1 wk for Console integration.
Open decision: whether to allow partial rollforward (profile fields) vs full manifest replacement. Eng leaning towards full-manifest atomic rollforward to simplify runtime compatibility checks.
